question: Should the OpenGrep security workflows adopt the 10-second connection and 120-second transfer deadlines, accepting fast CI failure during unusually prolonged installer-host slowness?
rationale: The patch changes a protected security workflow's download-and-execution behavior and makes a deliberate availability tradeoff that requires owner acceptance even though the implementation is otherwise sound.

options.title: Approve after guard correction
options.body: Accept the bounded-failure tradeoff after the regression guard explicitly checks both `-o "$opengrep_install"` and `bash "$opengrep_install"`.

options.title: Choose different deadlines
options.body: Retain the download-to-file approach but select longer limits if 120 seconds is too aggressive for expected runner conditions.

options.title: Keep current behavior
options.body: Decline the bounded fetch and continue relying on the workflow's outer timeout for installer-host stalls.

recommendation.title: Approve after guard correction
recommendation.body: Accept the bounded-failure tradeoff after the regression guard explicitly checks both `-o "$opengrep_install"` and `bash "$opengrep_install"`.

likelyOwner.reason: This person introduced and validated the OpenGrep security workflow design now being modified.
